record.name: People's Republic of China
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. CnAISDA conducts frontier AI safety evaluation research and international dialogue with reported government support, but no government designation of it as a national institute was found.

related_bodies.name: China AI Safety and Development Association (CnAISDA)
related_bodies.role: Tsinghua describes the association's frontier AI safety evaluation research and representation of China in international dialogue. It is a research network jointly created by Chinese universities, institutes and think tanks, with reported government support. No national government designation act was identified in the reviewed sources.

related_bodies.name: China Academy of Information and Communications Technology (CAICT)
related_bodies.role: It runs voluntary, opt-in AI safety benchmark evaluations with certificates through the industry alliance AIIA. It is a state research institute under the industry ministry.

related_bodies.name: TC260
related_bodies.role: It publishes the AI Safety Governance Framework. It is a national cybersecurity standards committee.

related_bodies.name: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC)
related_bodies.role: It runs security filing for generative AI services. It is an internet regulator.

check.language_note: The recorded zh queries use a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. English queries were also run on 17 October 2026; the previously recorded national or official-language coverage and its limits are unchanged. The additional status review used Chinese and English queries focused on national designation and later official acts; the network site was not freshly accessible. Search batches for the additional status review, using 1-based positions in check.searches: 19, 20; 21, 22, 23, 24. Each group records the same exact registered URLs found in its combined search results, without attribution to an individual query. Explicit page opens and finds and unverified URL variants are excluded. Groups list the recorded queries; some requests also contained additional queries retained in the research evidence.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.
check.governance_note: TC260's AI Safety Governance Framework 3.0, retrieved from the CAC website, recommends national standards and risk classification by sector regulators. Tsinghua documents the research network, while a government-hosted account reports support for its formation with unclear chronology. None of these retrieved texts assigns the network a qualifying national institute role.

record.notes:
Borderline. Chinese-language primary accounts document government support, a collaborative network and frontier AI safety evaluation research. The network's own rendered site includes testing methods and audits in its research remit. These sources do not establish the government designation required by the tracker; they also do not prove that no designation exists. A standalone organisation, separate staff or budget, and already-published model tests are not status requirements. Older secondary descriptions saying the network has no model-testing function of its own are dated reports and do not exclude it now. Tsinghua dates its public debut to February 2025; this is not necessarily its constitution or designation date.

Tsinghua's Chinese account describes frontier-safety evaluation research and representation of China; its English account confirms CnAISDA organised the dialogue. The Zhejiang government-hosted speech reports government support for formation. No national designation act was identified. An essay by Zhao Yifan of the Xi Jinping Economic Thought Research Centre, first published in 科技中国 (2025, no. 7) and reposted on the NDRC website on 3 December 2025, recommends exploring government AI safety institutes. The repost identifies the original journal issue but gives no exact original publication date. This attributed commentary does not identify a commissioned study or review of the option, an appointed advisory inquiry, or an adopted government proposal. Its call for domestic AI safety institutes to join international cooperation does not name or designate such a body. The uncertainty is government designation, not whether a network can qualify or whether it has published evaluations.

closest_body.name: China AI Safety and Development Association (CnAISDA)
closest_body.note: Tsinghua's English account names CnAISDA as the China AI Safety and Development Association; the Chinese account calls it a research network. A reproduced magazine piece on a government site, with an unidentified speaker and date, reports government support for its formation, and Tsinghua describes frontier AI safety evaluation research and international representation. No national assignment was identified. The support account's chronology remains unclear.

claims.text: CnAISDA says it conducts and supports research on "all aspects of AI safety, from theoretical foundations to testing methods, audits, governance and social impacts".
